chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father or from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from one of his men, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man came to him and said to him, 'May I be your ransom. What do you think of two young men who were lying together, so a son was born to this one and a girl to this one and a girl to the other. Can the son of this one marry the daughter of this one?' He said, 'Yes, Glory be to Allah, why should it not be permissible?' He said, 'He was a friend of his.' He said, 'And even if he was, there is no problem.' He said, 'But, he was doing it with him.' He said, 'So he turned his face away from him, then answered him while he was veiling with his arms, and said, 'If that which was from him was less than penetration, then there is no problem if they marry, but if he had penetrated, then it is not permissible for them to marry.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for the son of two men who had sex with each other to marry each other's daughter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the nuance of *ikhab* (penetration) in determining the severity of sodomy and its impact on marital eligibility (*kafa'ah*) between the families of the two partners. The Imam’s initial permissibility followed by restriction upon confirmation of penetration highlights that the act's physical consummation renders the parties less suitable for marriage to each other's offspring, reflecting the principle that moral severity affects social standing. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the specific nature of the sin influences familial alliances, distinguishing between mere companionship and full consummation.
